request.raw_text: Add third rotor blade to the assembly. It should have the same design as the other two. Radii should applied on all four long edges of the blade. Adjust central portion of all three blades so that there is a space for a new blade - reduce thickness of the central portion to cca 0,42mm. New blade should go through the center of the stack.

intention_words: same design as the other two
so that there is a space for a new blade

areas_to_change.action: Create and add a third rotor-blade member by duplicating the established blade design.
areas_to_change.reference_geometry: The two existing elongated rotor blades crossing at the central hub.
areas_to_change.location: In the rotor plane and within the central blade stack.
areas_to_change.description: Add one additional double-ended blade member with the same overall length, width, end profile, hole features, and general construction as the two existing blades.

areas_to_change.action: Position the new blade through the center of the stack.
areas_to_change.reference_geometry: Central hub, existing blade intersection, and blade stack.
areas_to_change.location: At the common rotor center, occupying the newly created intermediate stack space.
areas_to_change.description: Align the new blade's longitudinal centerline through the common center of the existing assembly. Place its central portion between the other blade layers without shifting the rotor center.

areas_to_change.action: Reduce the thickness of the central portions to approximately 0.42 mm.
areas_to_change.reference_geometry: Central overlapping portions of all three blades.
areas_to_change.location: Only within the region where the blades pass through and overlap at the central stack.
areas_to_change.description: Thin the local central section of each blade to approximately 0.42 mm so three blade members can occupy the stack while retaining their original thickness away from the hub. Provide suitable transitions between the thin central region and the full-thickness arms.

areas_to_change.reference_geometry: All four long edges of the blade.
areas_to_change.location: Along the two longitudinal sides on both major faces of the applicable blade member.
areas_to_change.description: Round the four lengthwise edges while preserving the blade's end geometry and central interface features. The requested radius value is not specified.

areas_to_preserve.reference_geometry: Existing central square hub or housing
areas_to_preserve.preservation_rule: Preserve its external rounded-square profile, position, overall dimensions, and relationship to the rotor center unless local clearance is strictly required.
Preserve their length, width, planar shape, full-thickness regions, rounded or angled end profiles, and end-hole geometry.
Keep the common center and rotation axis fixed; all three blade centerlines must intersect this axis.

areas_to_preserve.reference_geometry: Existing connectors, pins, collars, and central mounting features
areas_to_preserve.preservation_rule: Retain their geometry, alignment, and assembly relationships except where blade-layer spacing must accommodate the third central section.
Keep the blade arms in the established rotor plane, with only the thin central overlap portions separated through the stack thickness.

predicted_final_outcome.geometry: The assembly will contain three matching elongated blade members intersecting at one common center. Because each member extends through the center, the plan view will show six radial arms. The three locally thinned central portions will be layered through the hub stack, and the specified longitudinal edges will be rounded.
predicted_final_outcome.function: The revised central stack will provide clearance for the additional blade while retaining the existing hub, blade reach, mounting features, and rotor axis.
predicted_final_outcome.behavior: All three blade members will remain centered on the same rotation axis and rotate as one assembly, with reduced central thickness preventing geometric interference between the stacked blades.

ambiguities.description: The angular orientation of the third blade is not specified.
candidate_interpretations: Space all three blade centerlines uniformly, producing 60-degree separation between adjacent double-ended members and six equally spaced radial arms.
Place the third blade at any currently open angle while preserving the existing angular relationship of the first two blades.
Reorient all three blades to create a symmetric rotor pattern.

ambiguities.description: No numerical value is given for the radii on the four long edges.
candidate_interpretations: Match an existing longitudinal edge radius on the current blades.
Use the largest practical radius consistent with blade thickness.
Apply a separately specified manufacturing fillet radius.

ambiguities.description: It is unclear whether the four-long-edge radius requirement applies only to the new blade or to all three blades.
candidate_interpretations: Apply the radii only to the newly added blade.
Apply matching radii to all three blades to maintain identical designs.

ambiguities.description: The exact longitudinal extent and transition shape of the reduced-thickness central portion are not specified.
candidate_interpretations: Match the extent and transition geometry of the existing stepped central portions.
Thin only the minimum overlap length needed inside the hub.
Use gradual radiused or ramped transitions from 0.42 mm to the original blade thickness.

ambiguities.description: The term 'cca 0,42mm' indicates an approximate thickness without tolerance.
candidate_interpretations: Set each blade's central portion to exactly 0.42 mm nominal thickness.
Use approximately 0.42 mm and adjust slightly to satisfy stack clearance.
Interpret 0.42 mm as the total available thickness rather than the thickness of each blade central portion.
